newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares shrugged off initial weakness to close higher on Friday after Wall Street staged a recovery from yesterday's fall in early U.S. trade.
The AEX share index ended 8.03 points higher at 766.06 after hitting a low of 747.72 earlier.
Dealers said that the market had been volatile, but the fall in U.S. February producer prices had dispelled fears of an imminent U.S. interest rate hike.
"This, together with a recovery on Wall Street, gave the market a boost," said one dealer.
The dealer said the optimistic approach to the new U.S. figure was somewhat overdone.
"We just have to wait and see if wall Street keeps on its feet and to me it is not a good moment to step into the market as share prices are very high," he said.
Insurer Aegon rose 3.50 guilders to close at an all time high of 140.30. Aegon will announce its 1996 net next Friday.
Other financials also ended higher after early weakness.
Publisher Wolters Kluwer rose 2.10 guilders to 253.60. The stock recovered near the close since investors were digesting their disappointment as some had expected a share split.
Wolters Kluwer reported a six percent profit rise this morning to 479 million guilders and said it would raise its dividend pay-out ratio to 35 percent.
Electronics firm Philips slipped for the third day in a row and ended 1.50 guilders lower at 85.90, well under its high of 94.70 guilders dating from March 6.

Builder Volker Stevin - which announced a 1996 net profit rise of 25 percent this morning - gained 1.40 guilders to 201.50. Volker's intended merger partner Kondor Wessels rose 1.20 guilders to 89.00, after a rise in half-year results and upbeat forecast for its 1996/97 year results.
Brewer Heineken gained 8.50 guilders to 338.00, after announcing slightly lower results for 1996.
The net profit of 655 million guilders was just above analysts expectations and the stock was also supported by the news that the brewer forecast a profit growth for 1997.
Rival brewer Grolsch, which took a less upbeat approach to the current year when it warned of lower 1997 results, added 0.30 guilders to 60.80 today.
Grolsch fell 15 guilders to 59.00 on Wednesday after the profit warning and announcement of bleak 1996 results.
